findings.source_passage: many of whom yet carry on their bones unholy flesh. It makes a stranger stare.
findings.why_it_matters: The phrase 'carry on their bones unholy flesh' is a rhetorically charged, distinctively Melvillean formulation that intensifies the cannibal motif; its excision flattens the passage's shock effect.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'many of whom yet carry on their bones unholy flesh' immediately after 'savages outright' before 'It makes a stranger stare.'

findings.source_passage: No town-bred dandy will compare with a country-bred one—I mean a downright bumpkin dandy—a fellow that, in the dog-days, will mow his two acres in buckskin gloves for fear of tanning his hands.
findings.why_it_matters: The elaborated comic definition—'a fellow that, in the dog-days, will mow his two acres in buckskin gloves'—is the satirical payoff of the dandy passage and establishes the narrator's ironic register; its compression to 'a downright bumpkin' erases the joke.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full appositive definition including the buckskin-gloves detail, as it is the signature comic beat of the paragraph.

findings.source_passage: In summer time, the town is sweet to see; full of fine maples—long avenues of green and gold.
findings.why_it_matters: The summer/maples image and the candelabra simile work together as a lyrical pastoral set-piece; cutting the maples line reduces the passage to a single compressed image and loses the seasonal/chromatic build-up that gives the horse-chestnut sentence its resonance.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'In summer time, the town is sweet to see; full of fine maples—long avenues of green and gold' before the horse-chestnut sentence.

findings.source_passage: Whence came they? how planted upon this once scraggy scoria of a country?
findings.why_it_matters: These rhetorical questions set up the iconic harpoon-mansion answer in the next paragraph; without them the transition loses its interrogative momentum and the answer feels unmotivated.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the two closing rhetorical questions at the end of the 'patrician-like houses' paragraph to preserve the call-and-response structure.

findings.source_passage: In New Bedford, fathers, they say, give whales for dowers to their daughters
findings.why_it_matters: The draft drops 'to their daughters,' a small but rhythmically and tonally complete element of the satirical social portrait; 'give whales for dowers' alone is slightly truncated.
findings.suggested_fix: Minor: restore 'to their daughters' after 'give whales for dowers' for rhythmic completeness.

summary: No high-severity losses; three medium findings (unholy flesh phrase cut, bumpkin-dandy definition flattened, summer-maples opening absent) and two low findings reduce voice texture but no single loss is severe enough to require regeneration.
